findings.text: `source < existing_source` compares `ParameterSource` members, and `ParameterSource` is a plain `enum.Enum`, not an `IntEnum`, so it defines no ordering. Any second parameter that shares a name with an already-processed one, such as `--upper/--lower` with `flag_value` and `default=True`, raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'ParameterSource'`. This replaces the old skip-if-already-set behaviour for feature-switch groups, so it is a crash on a normal path.

Even if the enum were made orderable, the declaration order puts PROMPT last, so a prompted value ranks as less explicit than DEFAULT. In a shared-name group, an option that prompted the user would lose its slot to another option that merely fell back to its default.

When an option loses arbitration, its `consume_value` and `process_value` still run, but its source is never recorded. With `expose_value=False` or a UNSET existing value, the slot can be claimed by whichever option ran later, so `get_parameter_source` reflects the last writer rather than the actual winner.
